romanization.name: Hanyu Pinyin with tone marks
rules: Tone marks: ā first (high, level), á second (rising), ǎ third (dipping), à fourth (falling). No mark is the neutral tone.
Two third tones in a row: the first is said as a second tone. 你好 is written nǐ hǎo and said ní hǎo.
Typed answers may leave out the tone marks.

profile.formality: 你 is the everyday you. 您 is respectful: for elders, teachers, customers. Verbs do not change with either.
profile.script: Simplified characters, one syllable each. Four tones plus a neutral tone change the meaning.
profile.questionWords: 什么 (what), 哪儿 (where), 什么时候 (when), 谁 (who), 为什么 (why), 怎么 (how), 几 / 多少 (how many)
profile.agreement: No gender or number agreement. A number needs a measure word before a noun: 两个人, 三口人.
profile.conjugation: Verbs never change. Time and aspect come from words such as 了, 过, 在.
profile.wordOrder: Subject–verb–object. Time and place come before the verb: 我明天在北京工作.
